source: Thomas explicitly approved the two proposed A transfers in the Codex chat for Academy PR #183 on 2026-11-22: “Freigabe für Kartenübernahmen erteilt”
neighbouring_grade_review: The legacy Grade 6 Europe cell overlaps Geo7, and the approval includes its Ural Mountains retrieval. The legacy Grade 8 tropics and deserts cell is outside the Grade 7 scope.

rows.reason: The old answer says the downgoing plate melts; the new explanation models mantle melting and the complex Mediterranean setting.
The new course divides tectonic setting, volcanoes, hazards and monitoring between different tasks. The old synthesis also implies an overly uniform Mediterranean mechanism.
Both cards retrieve the North Atlantic Current as the continuation of the Gulf Stream system towards northwestern Europe. The new wording drops the absolute claim about ice-free ports.
The old prompt combines climate controls and the EU. The Academy practices them independently.
Both questions ask for the mountain range at the conventional eastern boundary. The old answer mentions the Ural River as additional context.
The old card requires a single long topographic synthesis including mountains, peninsulas, straits and six capitals. The course distributes orientation over several lessons.

The recall overlaps, but the old answer expressly requires rising sea level following glacial retreat. The new card retrieves glacial carving and later flooding without committing to that local mechanism.
The new course treats topography, climate and agriculture in separate tasks instead of reproducing the four-region synthesis.
The old answer requires three specific consequences of tourism-related groundwater use. The new package distributes these mechanisms across water use and coastal tourism.
The tourism prompt spans regional examples and several types of effects. No new card retains the whole retrieval.
The old prompt equates Schengen and EU membership and implies no checks in all cases. The new package distinguishes the two and does not repeat that retrieval.
The new card covers the four Single Market freedoms. It does not also retrieve the full history, currency and EU symbols.
